definition: The serene, unearned confidence with which a machine delivers an invented fact.
etymology: From confabulation — the psychiatric term for fabricated memories recounted sincerely (Latin confabulari, ‘to talk together’) — with the ending of confidence (Latin fidere, ‘to trust’). A story set beside a trust.
in_use: Ask it for case law and you get pure confabulence: citations that never existed, delivered like gospel.
the_case: It points at the right signal: the danger is not a wrong answer but a wrong answer told well, in the same even voice as every true one.
seo_title: confabulence: when a machine invents a fact with confidence
seo_description: The serene, unearned confidence with which a machine delivers an invented fact: the wrong answer told well, in the same even voice as every true one.
